questions.q: 10,000 voters vote to elect their mayor. A receives 500 votes more than that of B and wins the election. $5\%$ of the votes are invalid. If a news TV channel predicts that after 5 years the number of voters will increase by $50\%$ and A will receive $10\%$ votes less than that he received now, how many votes will B get at that time? (Assume all the votes as valid after 5 years and only A and B stand in the election in both the time)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling / JSM Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, linear calculations hain. Total vote aur winning margin diya ho toh dono candidates ke vote verbally add/subtract karke nikalne aane chahiye. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Pehle present data nikal. 10,000 ka $5\%$ (500) invalid ho gaye. Valid bache $9500$. Ab A aur B me equation banegi: $A + B = 9500$ aur margin $A - B = 500$. Dono equations ko add karega toh $2A = 10000 \implies A = 5000$. Matlab B ko abhi $4500$ mile hain. TV prediction pe aa: 5 saal baad total voters $50\%$ badh jayenge (sab valid) = $15000$. A ko pichle bar se $10\%$ kam vote milenge, yani $5000$ ka $90\% = 4500$. B ke vote nikalne ke liye bache hue vote pakad: $15000 - 4500 = 10500$ vote! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ek ek ko variables me assume karega toh confuse ho jayega. Values round hain toh sidha data pe khel. Exam Takeaway: Sum and Difference equations ($x+y=A, x-y=B$) ko mentally solve karna seekho.

questions.q: Doll's Math's test consists of 115 questions from three sections- i.e. A, B and C. 15 questions from section A, 40 questions from section B and 60 questions from section C. Although, she answered 66.67% of section A, 60% of section B and 50% of section C correctly. She did not pass the test because she got less than 60% of the total marks. How many more questions would she have to answer correctly to earn 60% of the marks, if each question's mark is 1?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, $66.67\%$ yani $\frac{2}{3}$. A, B, aur C ke sahi questions nikal aur 115 ke $60\%$ se compare kar le.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Direct parts nikal kar add kar aur target se subtract maar. Mathematically :-

$\text{Marks} = (15 \times \frac{2}{3}) + (40 \times \frac{3}{5}) + (60 \times \frac{1}{2})$

$\text{Marks} = 10 + 24 + 30 = 64$

$\text{Target} = 115 \times \frac{3}{5} = 69$

$\text{Diff} = 69 - 64 = 5$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Total questions aur percentages ko thoda detail mein evaluate kar. Mathematically :-

$A_{correct} = \frac{66.67}{100} \times 15 = 10$

$B_{correct} = \frac{60}{100} \times 40 = 24$

$C_{correct} = \frac{50}{100} \times 60 = 30$

$\text{Total Correct} = 64$

$\text{Req} = \frac{60}{100} \times 115 = 69 \Rightarrow 69 - 64 = 5$

Exam Takeaway: Percentages ki standard fraction values tips par yaad rakh, SSC CGL mein seedha 10-15 seconds bachenge.

questions.q: P's monthly salary is 60,000. He spends $45\%$ of his monthly salary on food and $25\%$ of the remaining monthly salary on house rent. Additionally, he spends X on children's education and spends $15\%$ of his monthly salary on travel. If he saved his remaining salary and his savings is 12,000 then find the value of X?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, 'remaining' aur 'monthly salary' keywords me fas gaya toh game over. Dhyan se dekh rent 'remaining' ka pucha hai, baki total ka!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Calculation dekho! Base salary $60$k. Food pe $45\%$ gaya yani $27$k. Bacha kitna? $33$k. Is bache hue ka $25\%$ (yani $\frac{1}{4}$) rent pe de diya $= 8250$. Travel par wapas total salary ka $15\%$ gaya yani $9000$. Total kharch $= 27000 + 8250 + 9000 = 44250$. Salary me se ye ghata toh $15750$ bacha. Usne $12000$ save kiye, matlab $15750 - 12000 = 3750$ bache, jo X (Education) ki value hai!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Tree method bana le. Total $100$ maan le. Food $45$. Bacha $55$. Rent $55 \times \frac{1}{4} = 13.75$. Travel $15$. Total $45 + 13.75 + 15 = 73.75$. Remaining $26.25$ units. Value daalke percentage se multiply karega toh bhi same aayega par direct values lena yahan better tha kyunki $60$k asaan number hai.

Exam Takeaway: Question padhte waqt aankhein eagle jaisi honi chahiye, 'remaining' word jahan likha ho wahi game palat jata hai.

questions.q: In an election only two candidates contested. 70% of the voters casted their votes and 425 casted votes declared invalid. Winner got 980 valid votes more than his opponent, if the number of valid votes received by the winner 38% of the number of registered total voters, then find how many registered voters cast their votes?
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, tree diagram bana dimaag me. 100x base. Cast 70x. Valid = 70x - 425. Winner le gaya 38x. Loser ko bacha 32x - 425. Margin (Winner - Loser) = 6x + 425 = 980. Toh 6x = 555. Pucha kya hai? Casted votes (70x). Agar 6x = 555, toh 70x direct nikal le.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Equation based margin solving.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Reg} = 100x, \quad \text{Cast} = 70x, \quad \text{Valid} = 70x - 425 \\ W = 38x \implies L = 70x - 425 - 38x = 32x - 425 \\ W - L = 980 \implies 38x - (32x - 425) = 980 \\ 6x + 425 = 980 \implies 6x = 555 \implies x = 92.5 \\ \text{Casted} = 70x = 70 \times 92.5 = 6475 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Direct value logic without x.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Total Valid Votes} = W + L \\ L = W - 980 \\ \text{Valid} = W + (W - 980) = 2W - 980 \\ \text{We know, Valid} = 70\% - 425 \text{ and } W = 38\% \\ 70\% - 425 = 2(38\%) - 980 \\ 70\% - 425 = 76\% - 980 \\ 6\% = 555 \\ 70\% = \frac{555}{6} \times 70 = 92.5 \times 70 = 6475 $$

Exam Takeaway: Election format me jab margin absolute terms me ho, waha percentages ki basic equation magic ki tarah kaam karti hai.

questions.q: Marks: Eng 45/50; Maths 70/100; Sci 40/50; Hist 55/100. Approx cumulative percentage?
questions.s:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 3. JSM (Junior Satisfaction Method) / Deviation

**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai, yaha base bahut simple hain (50 aur 100). Seedha add karna, percentage ya deviation nikalne se jyada fast hai. Total 300 base round figure me baith raha hai.

**Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Total marks acquired = $45 + 70 + 40 + 55 = 210$. Total maximum marks = $50 + 100 + 50 + 100 = 300$. Cumulative percentage = $\frac{210}{300} \times 100 = 70\%$. Ekdum bachho wala sawal hai!

**Method 2 (Concept Builder):** Agar base ajeeb hote toh hum individual percentage (90\%, 70\%, 80\%, 55\%) nikal kar weighted average ya JSM lagate, par jab direct adding aasan ho, toh apna ego side me rakh kar seedha jodo.

**Exam Takeaway:** DI (Data Interpretation) me pehle denominator check kiya kar, agar simple sum 100, 200, 300 ban raha ho toh shortcuts ki jagah normal addition hi fast hota hai.

questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Fraction fraction khelna hai bas, base same kar LCM leke.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Sidha fraction difference le: $7/8 - 3/5 = 11/40$. Yani jar ka $11/40$ part $= 3.2$ L. Total $= (3.2 \times 40)/11 = 128/11 = 11.6363...$ L. Options me $11.64$ clear match hai.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): LCM 40 maan le. Pehle 24 litre bhara tha, ab 35 litre bhara. Fark aaya 11 unit ka jo 3.2 L ke barabar hai. Total 40 unit nikalne ke liye Unitary method laga.

Exam Takeaway: Fractions ke questions me hamesha denominators ka LCM assume karke kaam aasan hota hai.

questions.q: In a group of 50 people, 28 have traveled to Europe, 31 have traveled to Asia, and 10 have traveled to both continents. How many people have not traveled to either continent?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 3. JSM / Deviation (Set Theory) Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, basic Venn diagram ya Set Theory ka sawal hai. Values choti hain, pen ki zaroorat hi nahi, mind me hi add-subtract kar. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total log jo kahin na kahin gaye hain = Europe + Asia - Both. Yani $28 + 31 - 10 = 49$. Total log group me $50$ the. Toh kitne log kahin nahi gaye? Seedha $50 - 49 = 1$. Secondon ka game hai! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Venn Diagram imagine kar. Beech me 'Both' wale $10$ rakh. 'Only Europe' wale bache $28 - 10 = 18$. 'Only Asia' wale bache $31 - 10 = 21$. Ab sabko jod le: Only E (18) + Only A (21) + Both (10) = 49. Total 50 me se 49 gaye toh bacha sirf 1. Aise concept build hota hai. Exam Takeaway: Jab tak 3 set wala sawal na ho, Venn diagram mat banana. Seedha $n(A \cup B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A \cap B)$ lagaya kar.

questions.q: The ratio of savings of two individuals is 6: 5. If one increases his savings by $15\%$ and the other by $10\%$, find their new savings ratio. (PHASE XIII(HS) - $\frac{28}{07}$/2025 - SHIFT 2)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 4. Cross-Product Method / Ratio Scaling Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ratios ke sath percentage me khelna ho toh base bada kar liya kar. 6 aur 5 ko seedha 60 aur 50, ya 600 aur 500 maan le. Calculation pen-free ho jayegi. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Savings maan le 60 aur 50. Pehle me $15\%$ bada, toh naya $60 \times 1.15 = 69$ hua. Dusre me $10\%$ bada, toh $50 \times 1.10 = 55$ hua. Naya ratio $69 : 55$ ban gaya. Dono prime-like category me phas rahe hain, kisi se nahi katega, isliye yahi final answer hai! Option B seedha thokh! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ratio me variables lagao: $6x$ aur $5x$. New ratio banega $(6x \times \frac{115}{100}) : (5x \times \frac{110}{100})$. $100$ se $100$ aur $x$ se $x$ cut jayega. Bacha $(6 \times 115) : (5 \times 110) = 690 : 550$. Zero cut karke $69 : 55$ aagaya. Par mazdoori kyu karni jab direct number soch sakte ho? Exam Takeaway: Ratio values me jab percentage change aaye, zero chipka kar decimals ko avoid kiya kar.

questions.q: The cost of a table is 200% more than that of a chair and the cost of a chair is 20% less than that of a cupboard. If the price of each table and chair is decreased by 25%, and the price of a cupboard is increased by 25%, what will be the percentage increase/decrease in the total cost of 4 tables, 5 chairs and 8 shelves?
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, Shelf ko 100 man le. Chair 80 hogi. Table $200\%$ zyada yani $80+160=240$. Seedha items me multiply kar aur nayi cost nikal. Calculation sidhi hai koi JSM mat laga kyunki items and rates scattered hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Direct Ratio Mapping.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Shelf (S)} = 100, \quad \text{Chair (C)} = 80, \quad \text{Table (T)} = 240 \\ \text{Old Cost} = 4(240) + 5(80) + 8(100) = 960 + 400 + 800 = 2160 \\ \text{New T} = 240 \times 0.75 = 180 \\ \text{New C} = 80 \times 0.75 = 60 \\ \text{New S} = 100 \times 1.25 = 125 \\ \text{New Cost} = 4(180) + 5(60) + 8(125) = 720 + 300 + 1000 = 2020 \\ \text{Decrease} = 2160 - 2020 = 140 \\ \% = \frac{140}{2160} \times 100 = 6.48\% \approx 6.5\% \downarrow $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Variables ke form me value change.

Mathematically :-
$$ C = 0.8 S, \quad T = C + 2C = 3C = 2.4 S \\ \text{Old Total} = 4(2.4S) + 5(0.8S) + 8S = 9.6S + 4S + 8S = 21.6 S \\ T_{\text{new}} = 0.75(2.4S) = 1.8S \\ C_{\text{new}} = 0.75(0.8S) = 0.6S \\ S_{\text{new}} = 1.25S \\ \text{New Total} = 4(1.8S) + 5(0.6S) + 8(1.25S) = 7.2S + 3S + 10S = 20.2 S \\ \text{Drop} = \frac{21.6S - 20.2S}{21.6S} \times 100 = \frac{1.4}{21.6} \times 100 = 6.48\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Aise questions me base 100 assume karna aur straight line multiply karna hi best rehta hai. Jyada smart banne gaye toh fass jaoge.

questions.q: Every month, a man consumes 15 kg of rice and 6 kg of wheat. The price of rice is $20\%$ of the price of wheat, resulting in a total expenditure of 225 per month for rice and wheat combined. If the price of wheat is increased by $12\%$, what percentage reduction in rice consumption is needed to maintain the same expenditure of 225? (Given that price of rice and consumption of wheat is constant)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: CPR (Constant Product Ratio) / Unitary Scaling Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, price of Rice $20\%$ of Wheat hai, yani inka price ratio 1:5 hoga. Kharcha maintain karna hai toh idhar ka paisa udhar compensate karna padega. Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): R:W price ratio 1:5 hai. Maan le Rice Rs. $x$/kg, Wheat Rs. $5x$/kg. Total bill: $15(x) + 6(5x) = 45x$. Par total kharcha 225 diya hai $\implies 45x = 225 \implies x = 5$. Toh Rice = Rs. 5/kg, Wheat = Rs. 25/kg. Ab Wheat price 12% bada, yani $25 \times 0.12 = 3$ Rs badha per kg. 6 kg wheat pe Rs. 18 ka extra phatka. Total bill 225 hi rakhna hai toh ye 18 Rs Rice kam khakar bachana hoga. 1 kg Rice 5 ka hai. Kitna Rice kam aayega? $\frac{18}{5} = 3.6$ kg. Pehle rice khata tha 15 kg. Percentage reduction = $\frac{3.6}{15} \times 100 = 24\%$. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ek ek value ko fraction me handle kar, par equations lamba padenge. Focus on 'extra cost' compensation. Exam Takeaway: Expense maintaining wale sawalo me pura recalculate mat kar. Sirf "Extra Badha Hua Kharcha = Doosri taraf bachi hui unit" pe equate kar.

questions.q: A saves $40\%$ of his income and B saves $20\%$ more than A. If the income of A is $80\%$ of the income of B and A's expenditure is $\text{Rs. } 18000$, then what is the expenditure of B?
questions.s:
[Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling]

Pen-Free Observation: B ki income ko 100 aur A ki 80 maanke mind me structure bana. A ka expenditure $60\%$ of 80 yani 48 units banega jiski value 18000 hai.



Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Let B's income $= 100$.
A's income $= 80$.
A's saving $= 40\%$ of $80 = 32$.
A's exp $= 80 - 32 = 48$.
B's saving is $20\%$ MORE than A's saving $\Rightarrow 32 \times 1.2 = 38.4$.
B's exp $= 100 - 38.4 = 61.6$.
Question me $48 \text{ units} = 18000 \Rightarrow 1 \text{ unit} = 375$.
B's exp $= 61.6 \times 375 = 23100$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Decimals se dar lagta hai toh $61.6 \times 375$ ko $61.6 \times \frac{3000}{8}$ likh le. Seedha $7.7 \times 3000 = 23100$ aayega. Calculation fast karne ke liye fractions ka use ekdum best hai.

questions.q:
A farm cultivates Maize and Soybeans. The ratio of the land area allocated to Maize and Soybeans is 3:2. Initially, both crops yield the exact same amount of produce per acre.

This year, the land area for Maize was increased by 25% but its yield per acre dropped by 4%. Meanwhile, the area for Soybeans was increased by 40% but its yield per acre plummeted by 30%. What is the overall percentage change in the total farm production?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change + Weighted Average (JSM) Pen-Free Observation: Yahan koi total fix nahi hai, sab kuch badal raha hai aur final overall change pucha hai. Pehle dono fasalon ka alag-alag net successive nikal. Maize ka area badha aur yield ghata ($+25, -4$), iska successive aayega $+20\%$. Soybeans ka ($+40, -30$), successive aaya $-2\%$. Ab in dono percentages ko inke initial production base ratio ($3:2$) par JSM se mila de. Total deviation nikal aur total base se divide maar! Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Successive nikal kar direct JSM (Weighted Average) laga. Mathematically :-
$\text{Production Ratio (Maize : Soy)} = (3 \times 1) : (2 \times 1) = 3 : 2$
$\text{Maize Net Change} = 25 - 4 - \frac{25 \times 4}{100} = +20\%$
$\text{Soybeans Net Change} = 40 - 30 - \frac{40 \times 30}{100} = -2\%$
$\text{Net Deviation} = (3 \times 20) + (2 \times -2) = 60 - 4 = +56$
$\text{Overall \% Change} = \frac{+56}{3 + 2} = \frac{56}{5} = +11.2\%$ Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute data assume karke final total nikalna. Mathematically :-
$\text{Let Area (Maize = 300, Soy = 200) and Yield = 10 units/acre}$
$\text{Initial Prod} = (300 \times 10) + (200 \times 10) = 3000 + 2000 = 5000$
$\text{New Maize Prod} = (300 \times 1.25) \times (10 \times 0.96) = 375 \times 9.6 = 3600$
$\text{New Soy Prod} = (200 \times 1.40) \times (10 \times 0.70) = 280 \times 7 = 1960$
$\text{Total New Prod} = 3600 + 1960 = 5560$
$\% \text{ Change} = \frac{5560 - 5000}{5000} \times 100 = 11.2\%$ Exam Takeaway: Successive aur JSM SSC/CDS ke sabse powerful core tools hain. Jab variables multiple dimensions me change hon, toh hamesha unhe Successive se ek single 1D percentage me sikod lo, aur uske baad normal JSM/Average laga lo.
Data ComponentTool Applied
Individual Crop ($Area \times Yield$)Successive Change
Overall Farm ($Crop_1 + Crop_2$)JSM / Weighted Average

questions.q: In an exam, 44% of students passed in only History and 36% of students passed in only Economics. If 6% of the students failed in both subjects and the number of students who failed in Economics is 125, then find the number of students who failed in History.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Venn diagram banane ka time waste bilkul nahi karna. 'Failed in Economics' ka direct matlab hota hai wo students jo sirf History me pass hue hain plus jo dono me nipat gaye (failed in both). Data dekhte hi percentages dimag me add hone chahiye.



Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Failed in Economics = (Passed in Only History) + (Failed in Both). Yaani $44\% + 6\% = 50\%$. Question cheekh-cheekh ke keh raha hai ki ye $50\%$ ki value 125 bacche hai. Toh multiplier kya hua? $125 / 50 = 2.5$ times. Ab hume nikalna hai 'Failed in History', jo hoga (Passed in Only Economics) + (Failed in Both) = $36\% + 6\% = 42\%$. Toh actual value nikalne ke liye Unitary Scaling lagao: $42 \times 2.5 = 105$. Khel khatam, 10-15 seconds me ans mark kar aur aage badh!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Let Total students = $100x$. Only History (H) = $44x$, Only Economics (E) = $36x$, Failed Both = $6x$. Passed in Both = $100x - (44x + 36x + 6x) = 14x$. 'Failed in Economics' ka matalab wo jo E circle ke bahar hain = Only H + Failed Both = $44x + 6x = 50x$. Given $50x = 125 \implies x = 2.5$. We need 'Failed in History' = Only E + Failed Both = $36x + 6x = 42x$. Therefore, actual count = $42 \times 2.5 = 105$.

Future Exam Takeaway: SSC CGL aur CDS me jab bhi 'Failed in Subject A' pooche, toh ek golden rule raat le: Failed in A = Only Pass in B + Fail in Both. Yeh single property Venn diagram ke questions ko bina circle draw kiye verbally uda deti hai.

questions.q: A fruit seller had total (X+50) mangoes and apples. He sold 20% mangoes to A, 40% of remaining to B and had 48 mangoes left. Similarly, he sold 40% apples to A, 100 apples to B and had 10% apples left. Find (X+500).
questions.s:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai, dono fruits ka track ek dum alag hai, mangoes me seedha percentage successive hai aur apples me percentage ke beech absolute number (100) mixed hai. Dono ko alag alag handle kar!

**Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Mangoes(M): 20\% bika (bacha 80\%), fir 40\% bika (bacha 60\%). Equate kar de: $M \times 0.8 \times 0.6 = 48 \implies 0.48M = 48 \implies M = 100$.
Apples(A): 40\% becha toh bacha 60\%. Ab isme se 100 beche toh end me 10\% bache. Equation bani $0.6A - 100 = 0.1A \implies 0.5A = 100 \implies A = 200$. Total fruits (X+50) hue $100+200 = 300$. Yaha se X = 250 aaya. Pucha X+500 hai, yani $250+500 = 750$.

**Successive Change (The Chain Reaction) & Unitary Scaling.

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dekh bhai, Mangoes aur Apples dono ke events bilkul independent hain. Exam me variable `X` dekh kar ghabrana nahi hai. Sabse best hack hai ki pehle individual fruits ki total sankhya percentage ya ratio se nikal lo, aur last me unko add karke `X+50` se equate kar do. Tune jo 3 methods diye hain, aao sabka post-mortem karte hain.

Method 1 (Percentage Base Shift - Ninja Technique):
Mangoes: Let total = 100\%.
Remaining after 20\% sold = 80\%.
Remaining after 40\% of 80\% sold = 80\% \times 60\% = 48\%.
ATQ, 48\% \equiv 48 \Rightarrow 100\% \equiv 100 mangoes.

Apples: Let total = 100\%.
Sold to A = 40\%. Bacha hua 60\%.
Ab isme se 100 apples B ko diye, toh 10\% bache.
Iska sidha observation hai: 60\% - 10\% = 50\%. Ye 50\% hi 100 apples ke barabar hain!
50\% \equiv 100 \Rightarrow 100\% \equiv 200 apples.

Total fruits = 100 + 200 = 300.
So, X + 50 = 300 \Rightarrow X = 250.
Find: X + 500 = 250 + 500 = 750.

Method 2 (Fractional Successive Ratio - Exam Approach):
Mangoes (Successive Change):
20\% = \frac{1}{5} (Base shift: 5 se 4), 40\% = \frac{2}{5} (Base shift: 5 se 3).
InitialFinal
54
53
2512
12 units \equiv 48 \Rightarrow 1 unit = 4.
Total Mangoes = 25 \times 4 = 100.

Apples (Direct Observation):
Total = 100\%. Sold to A = 40\%, Remaining = 10\%.
Consumed percentage without absolute value = 40\% + 10\% = 50\%.
Rest 50\% is exactly the 100 apples given to B.
50\% \equiv 100 \Rightarrow 100\% = 200.
Total = 300, X = 250, Ans = 750.

Method 3 (Basic Variable Equation - The Trap):
Ye teri 3rd image wala approach hai, jo ekdum basic hai. Exam me ye nahi lagana hai!
Mangoes = 100 (derived). Total fruits = X + 50.
So, Total Apples = (X + 50) - 100 = (X - 50).
ATQ for apples:
Sold 40\% (i.e. \frac{2}{5}), remaining = \frac{3}{5}.
(X - 50) \times \frac{3}{5} - 100 = (X - 50) \times \frac{1}{10}
(X - 50) \times \frac{3}{5} - (X - 50) \times \frac{1}{10} = 100
(X - 50) \times \frac{1}{2} = 100
(X - 50) = 200 \Rightarrow X = 250.
Bhai, isme expression balance karne me time jayega. It's a pure waste of 30-40 seconds.


Future Exam Takeaway (Hack Observation):
Exam me hamesha Method 1 ya 2 lagana hai. Jab question me do alag-alag items (Mangoes aur Apples) ho, toh starting ke combined variable (X+50) ko temporarily bhool jao. Individual parts ko 100\% base ya ratio base par solve karo, unki real values nikal kar last me combine karo. Variables ke jaal me tab tak nahi fasna jab tak strictly necessary na ho!

questions.q: Khushi scores $33.33\%$ in an examination and after review, even though her score is increased by $40\%$, she fails by 10 marks. If her post - review score is increased by $14.28\%$, she will have 10 marks more than the passing score. Find the percentage score needed for passing the examination.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, fraction ka khel hai. $33.33\%$ matlab $\frac{1}{3}$, $40\%$ matlab $\frac{2}{5}$ aur $14.28\%$ matlab $\frac{1}{7}$. Base aisi value maan jo in sabse kat jaye, jaise $300$! Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total marks $300$ maan le. Khushi ka score aaya $100$ unit. Usme $40\%$ badhaya toh ban gaya $140$ unit. Ye passing marks se $10$ kam hai. Passing = $140u + 10$. Phir is $140u$ ko $14.28\%$ (yani $\frac{1}{7}$) badhaya, toh $140 + 20 = 160$ unit hua. questions.q: If the price of rice is raised by $28\%$, then by how much percent must a person reduce his consumption of rice so that his overall expenditure remains the same?
questions.s:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, sidha CPR (Constant Product Ratio) laga. Jab fraction $+\frac{x}{y}$ se badhti hai aur product same rakhna ho, toh factor $-\frac{x}{x+y}$ se girana padta hai.

Method 1 (CPR Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Price } \uparrow = +28\% = +\frac{28}{100} = +\frac{7}{25} \\ \text{Consumption } \downarrow = -\frac{7}{25+7} = -\frac{7}{32} \\ \% \text{ Change} = \frac{7}{32} \times 100 = \frac{175}{8} = 21.875\% $$

questions.q: For a number, greater than one, the difference between itself and its reciprocal is 20% of the sum of itself and its reciprocal. By how much percentage (nearest to an integer) is the square of the number less than its cube?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, language thodi ghumau hai par basic algebraic equation ban rahi hai. Cross multiply karke seedha number ka square nikal lena sabse asaan hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Equation ko fraction ki tarah set kar, solve karke cube aur square ka ratio nikal de!

Mathematically :-
$$x - \frac{1}{x} = 0.2\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right) \implies \frac{x - \frac{1}{x}}{x + \frac{1}{x}} = \frac{1}{5}$$
$$5x - \frac{5}{x} = x + \frac{1}{x} \implies 4x = \frac{6}{x} \implies x^2 = 1.5$$
$$x = \sqrt{1.5} \approx 1.2247$$
$$\text{Req } \% = \frac{x^3 - x^2}{x^3} \times 100 = \left(1 - \frac{1}{x}\right) \times 100$$
$$\left(1 - \frac{1}{1.2247}\right) \times 100 \approx (1 - 0.816) \times 100 \approx 18.3\% \approx 18\%$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute values pe ja kar cube nikalega aur square nikalega toh decimals me jaakar puri tarah fass jayega. Seedha ratio utha.

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Req } \% = \frac{A-B}{A} \times 100 = \left(1 - \frac{B}{A}\right) \times 100$$

Exam Takeaway: Percentage less/more pooche algebra me toh hamesha unka ratio $\frac{A}{B}$ form me convert kar lo, original absolute values ki tension khatam ho jayegi.

Total strength = 25. Percentage = $\frac{10}{25} \times 100 = 40\%$.

**Method 2 (Concept Builder):** Fractions convert karke sidha remainder nikal. Agar $\frac{11}{16}$ chale gaye toh $\frac{5}{16}$ bach gaye. Arithmetic game sirf fractions ke base denominator ko target karne ka hota hai.

questions.q: The salaries of Prashant and Sujal together amount to 24000. Prashant spends (x - 5)% of his salary and Sujal, (x + 5)% of his. If ratio of their income is 3 : 5 and their savings are same, then what is difference between their expenditure?
questions.s:
Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, Income ratio 3:5 hai, total 8 unit = 24000. Toh Prashant = 9000, Sujal = 15000. Dono ki saving barabar hai. Agar Income ka gap 6000 hai aur savings same hain, toh Expenditure ka gap directly Income ke gap ke barabar hoga! Calculation ki zarurat hi nahi thi!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Logic aur Common Sense.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Income (P)} = \frac{3}{8} \times 24000 = 9000 \\ \text{Income (S)} = \frac{5}{8} \times 24000 = 15000 \\ \text{Income} = \text{Exp} + \text{Sav} \\ \text{If } \text{Sav}_P = \text{Sav}_S, \text{ then:} \\ \text{Inc}_S - \text{Inc}_P = \text{Exp}_S - \text{Exp}_P \\ \text{Diff} = 15000 - 9000 = 6000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Percentage equate karke x nikalna.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Sav}_P = 100 - (x - 5) = (105 - x)\% \\ \text{Sav}_S = 100 - (x + 5) = (95 - x)\% \\ 9000 \times (105 - x) = 15000 \times (95 - x) \\ 3(105 - x) = 5(95 - x) \implies 315 - 3x = 475 - 5x \\ 2x = 160 \implies x = 80 \\ \text{Exp}_P = 75\% \text{ of } 9000 = 6750 \\ \text{Exp}_S = 85\% \text{ of } 15000 = 12750 \\ \text{Diff} = 12750 - 6750 = 6000 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab savings same ho toh Income ka difference seedha Expenditure ke difference ke barabar hota hai. x nikalna bewakoofi thi!

questions.q: Ridhi scored 65 marks in Mathematics. He scored $70\%$ marks in Hindi and $(X^3 + 20)$ marks in English. The maximum marks for each subject is 80. The overall percentage of marks obtained by Riddhi in all three subjects together is $70\%$. Find X?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, overall average $70\%$ hai toh har subject me target marks set kar, jo average se extra laya usko dusre subjects se balance kar le.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Deviation Balance. Mathematically :-
$$Avg_{target} = 80 \times 0.70 = 56$$
$$H = 56 \text{ (0 dev)}$$
$$M = 65 \text{ (+9 dev)}$$
$$E_{target} = 56 - 9 = 47$$
$$X^3 + 20 = 47 \Rightarrow X^3 = 27 \Rightarrow X = 3$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Total Sum approach. Mathematically :-
$$Total = 80 \times 3 = 240$$
$$Obtained = 240 \times 0.70 = 168$$
$$65 + 56 + (X^3 + 20) = 168$$
$$141 + X^3 = 168 \Rightarrow X^3 = 27 \Rightarrow X=3$$

Exam Takeaway: Sabko add karke wapas minus karne se accha hai individual average deviation zero pe balance karna, isse calculation chhoti ho jati hai.

If his expenditure is increased by 12% on food and 15% on cloth and decreased by 8% on other items. What percent should his income be increased so that no effect is recorded on the consumption of food, cloth and other items ?
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ratios di hain 3:4:3. Inko sidha 300, 400 aur 300 maan le. Income base 1000 banega. Bas change nikal aur 1000 pe percentage fenk.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Zeroes assum kar aur base 1000 pe deviation nikal. Mathematically :-

$+ (400 \times 15\%) = +60$

$- (300 \times 8\%) = -24$

$\text{Net} = 36 + 60 - 24 = +72$

$\text{Inc } \% = \frac{72}{1000} \times 100 = 7.2\%$

$\text{Change} = \frac{(3 \times 12) + (4 \times 15) + (3 \times -8)}{10}$

$\text{Change} = \frac{36 + 60 - 24}{10} = \frac{72}{10} = 7.2\%$

Exam Takeaway: Jaha split ratio di ho waha zeros chipka ke life aasan kiya kar ya direct weighted average laga, fraction apne aap set hoga.

questions_hin.q_hi: In an election only two candidates contested. 70% of the voters casted their votes and 425 casted votes declared invalid. Winner got 980 valid votes more than his opponent, if the number of valid votes received by the winner 38% of the number of registered total voters, then find how many registered voters cast their votes?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, tree diagram bana dimaag me. 100x base. Cast 70x. Valid = 70x - 425. Winner le gaya 38x. Loser ko bacha 32x - 425. Margin (Winner - Loser) = 6x + 425 = 980. Toh 6x = 555. Pucha kya hai? Casted votes (70x). Agar 6x = 555, toh 70x direct nikal le.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Equation based margin solving.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Reg} = 100x, \quad \text{Cast} = 70x, \quad \text{Valid} = 70x - 425 \\ W = 38x \implies L = 70x - 425 - 38x = 32x - 425 \\ W - L = 980 \implies 38x - (32x - 425) = 980 \\ 6x + 425 = 980 \implies 6x = 555 \implies x = 92.5 \\ \text{Casted} = 70x = 70 \times 92.5 = 6475 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Direct value logic without x.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Total Valid Votes} = W + L \\ L = W - 980 \\ \text{Valid} = W + (W - 980) = 2W - 980 \\ \text{We know, Valid} = 70\% - 425 \text{ and } W = 38\% \\ 70\% - 425 = 2(38\%) - 980 \\ 70\% - 425 = 76\% - 980 \\ 6\% = 555 \\ 70\% = \frac{555}{6} \times 70 = 92.5 \times 70 = 6475 $$

Exam Takeaway: Election format me jab margin absolute terms me ho, waha percentages ki basic equation magic ki tarah kaam karti hai.

Zero cut karke $69 : 55$ aagaya. Par mazdoori kyu karni jab direct number soch sakte ho? Exam Takeaway: Ratio values me jab percentage change aaye, zero chipka kar decimals ko avoid kiya kar.

questions_hin.q_hi: The cost of a table is 200% more than that of a chair and the cost of a chair is 20% less than that of a cupboard. If the price of each table and chair is decreased by 25%, and the price of a cupboard is increased by 25%, what will be the percentage increase/decrease in the total cost of 4 tables, 5 chairs and 8 shelves?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, Shelf ko 100 man le. Chair 80 hogi. Table $200\%$ zyada yani $80+160=240$. Seedha items me multiply kar aur nayi cost nikal. Calculation sidhi hai koi JSM mat laga kyunki items and rates scattered hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Direct Ratio Mapping.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Shelf (S)} = 100, \quad \text{Chair (C)} = 80, \quad \text{Table (T)} = 240 \\ \text{Old Cost} = 4(240) + 5(80) + 8(100) = 960 + 400 + 800 = 2160 \\ \text{New T} = 240 \times 0.75 = 180 \\ \text{New C} = 80 \times 0.75 = 60 \\ \text{New S} = 100 \times 1.25 = 125 \\ \text{New Cost} = 4(180) + 5(60) + 8(125) = 720 + 300 + 1000 = 2020 \\ \text{Decrease} = 2160 - 2020 = 140 \\ \% = \frac{140}{2160} \times 100 = 6.48\% \approx 6.5\% \downarrow $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Variables ke form me value change.

Mathematically :-
$$ C = 0.8 S, \quad T = C + 2C = 3C = 2.4 S \\ \text{Old Total} = 4(2.4S) + 5(0.8S) + 8S = 9.6S + 4S + 8S = 21.6 S \\ T_{\text{new}} = 0.75(2.4S) = 1.8S \\ C_{\text{new}} = 0.75(0.8S) = 0.6S \\ S_{\text{new}} = 1.25S \\ \text{New Total} = 4(1.8S) + 5(0.6S) + 8(1.25S) = 7.2S + 3S + 10S = 20.2 S \\ \text{Drop} = \frac{21.6S - 20.2S}{21.6S} \times 100 = \frac{1.4}{21.6} \times 100 = 6.48\% $$

Exam Takeaway: Aise questions me base 100 assume karna aur straight line multiply karna hi best rehta hai. Jyada smart banne gaye toh fass jaoge.

Total bill: $15(x) + 6(5x) = 45x$. Par total kharcha 225 diya hai $\implies 45x = 225 \implies x = 5$. Toh Rice = Rs. 5/kg, Wheat = Rs. 25/kg. Kitna Rice kam aayega? $\frac{18}{5} = 3.6$ kg. Pehle rice khata tha 15 kg. Percentage reduction = $\frac{3.6}{15} \times 100 = 24\%$. Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ek ek value ko fraction me handle kar, par equations lamba padenge. Focus on 'extra cost' compensation. questions_hin.q_hi: A saves $40\%$ of his income and B saves $20\%$ more than A. If the income of A is $80\%$ of the income of B and A's expenditure is $\text{Rs. } 18000$, then what is the expenditure of B?
questions_hin.s_hi:
[Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling]

Pen-Free Observation: B ki income ko 100 aur A ki 80 maanke mind me structure bana. A ka expenditure $60\%$ of 80 yani 48 units banega jiski value 18000 hai.



Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Let B's income $= 100$.
A's income $= 80$.
A's saving $= 40\%$ of $80 = 32$.
A's exp $= 80 - 32 = 48$.
B's saving is $20\%$ MORE than A's saving $\Rightarrow 32 \times 1.2 = 38.4$.
B's exp $= 100 - 38.4 = 61.6$.
Question me $48 \text{ units} = 18000 \Rightarrow 1 \text{ unit} = 375$.
B's exp $= 61.6 \times 375 = 23100$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Decimals se dar lagta hai toh $61.6 \times 375$ ko $61.6 \times \frac{3000}{8}$ likh le. Seedha $7.7 \times 3000 = 23100$ aayega. Calculation fast karne ke liye fractions ka use ekdum best hai.

questions_hin.q_hi:
A farm cultivates Maize and Soybeans. The ratio of the land area allocated to Maize and Soybeans is 3:2. Initially, both crops yield the exact same amount of produce per acre.

This year, the land area for Maize was increased by 25% but its yield per acre dropped by 4%. Meanwhile, the area for Soybeans was increased by 40% but its yield per acre plummeted by 30%. What is the overall percentage change in the total farm production?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: Successive Change + Weighted Average (JSM) Pen-Free Observation: Yahan koi total fix nahi hai, sab kuch badal raha hai aur final overall change pucha hai. Pehle dono fasalon ka alag-alag net successive nikal. Maize ka area badha aur yield ghata ($+25, -4$), iska successive aayega $+20\%$. Soybeans ka ($+40, -30$), successive aaya $-2\%$. Ab in dono percentages ko inke initial production base ratio ($3:2$) par JSM se mila de. Total deviation nikal aur total base se divide maar! Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Successive nikal kar direct JSM (Weighted Average) laga. Mathematically :-
$\text{Production Ratio (Maize : Soy)} = (3 \times 1) : (2 \times 1) = 3 : 2$
$\text{Maize Net Change} = 25 - 4 - \frac{25 \times 4}{100} = +20\%$
$\text{Soybeans Net Change} = 40 - 30 - \frac{40 \times 30}{100} = -2\%$
$\text{Net Deviation} = (3 \times 20) + (2 \times -2) = 60 - 4 = +56$
$\text{Overall \% Change} = \frac{+56}{3 + 2} = \frac{56}{5} = +11.2\%$ Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute data assume karke final total nikalna. Mathematically :-
$\text{Let Area (Maize = 300, Soy = 200) and Yield = 10 units/acre}$
$\text{Initial Prod} = (300 \times 10) + (200 \times 10) = 3000 + 2000 = 5000$
$\text{New Maize Prod} = (300 \times 1.25) \times (10 \times 0.96) = 375 \times 9.6 = 3600$
$\text{New Soy Prod} = (200 \times 1.40) \times (10 \times 0.70) = 280 \times 7 = 1960$
$\text{Total New Prod} = 3600 + 1960 = 5560$
$\% \text{ Change} = \frac{5560 - 5000}{5000} \times 100 = 11.2\%$ Exam Takeaway: Successive aur JSM SSC/CDS ke sabse powerful core tools hain. Jab variables multiple dimensions me change hon, toh hamesha unhe Successive se ek single 1D percentage me sikod lo, aur uske baad normal JSM/Average laga lo.
Data ComponentTool Applied
Individual Crop ($Area \times Yield$)Successive Change
Overall Farm ($Crop_1 + Crop_2$)JSM / Weighted Average

questions_hin.q_hi: In an exam, 44% of students passed in only History and 36% of students passed in only Economics. If 6% of the students failed in both subjects and the number of students who failed in Economics is 125, then find the number of students who failed in History.
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Venn diagram banane ka time waste bilkul nahi karna. 'Failed in Economics' ka direct matlab hota hai wo students jo sirf History me pass hue hain plus jo dono me nipat gaye (failed in both). Data dekhte hi percentages dimag me add hone chahiye.



Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Failed in Economics = (Passed in Only History) + (Failed in Both). Yaani $44\% + 6\% = 50\%$. Question cheekh-cheekh ke keh raha hai ki ye $50\%$ ki value 125 bacche hai. Toh multiplier kya hua? $125 / 50 = 2.5$ times. Ab hume nikalna hai 'Failed in History', jo hoga (Passed in Only Economics) + (Failed in Both) = $36\% + 6\% = 42\%$. Toh actual value nikalne ke liye Unitary Scaling lagao: $42 \times 2.5 = 105$. Khel khatam, 10-15 seconds me ans mark kar aur aage badh!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Let Total students = $100x$. Only History (H) = $44x$, Only Economics (E) = $36x$, Failed Both = $6x$. Passed in Both = $100x - (44x + 36x + 6x) = 14x$. 'Failed in Economics' ka matalab wo jo E circle ke bahar hain = Only H + Failed Both = $44x + 6x = 50x$. Given $50x = 125 \implies x = 2.5$. We need 'Failed in History' = Only E + Failed Both = $36x + 6x = 42x$. Therefore, actual count = $42 \times 2.5 = 105$.

Future Exam Takeaway: SSC CGL aur CDS me jab bhi 'Failed in Subject A' pooche, toh ek golden rule raat le: Failed in A = Only Pass in B + Fail in Both. Yeh single property Venn diagram ke questions ko bina circle draw kiye verbally uda deti hai.

questions_hin.q_hi: A fruit seller had total (X+50) mangoes and apples. He sold 20% mangoes to A, 40% of remaining to B and had 48 mangoes left. Similarly, he sold 40% apples to A, 100 apples to B and had 10% apples left. Find (X+500).
questions_hin.s_hi:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 2. Successive Change (The Chain Reaction)

**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai, dono fruits ka track ek dum alag hai, mangoes me seedha percentage successive hai aur apples me percentage ke beech absolute number (100) mixed hai. Dono ko alag alag handle kar!

**Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** Mangoes(M): 20\% bika (bacha 80\%), fir 40\% bika (bacha 60\%). Equate kar de: $M \times 0.8 \times 0.6 = 48 \implies 0.48M = 48 \implies M = 100$.
Apples(A): 40\% becha toh bacha 60\%. Ab isme se 100 beche toh end me 10\% bache. Equation bani $0.6A - 100 = 0.1A \implies 0.5A = 100 \implies A = 200$. Total fruits (X+50) hue $100+200 = 300$. Yaha se X = 250 aaya. Pucha X+500 hai, yani $250+500 = 750$.

**Successive Change (The Chain Reaction) & Unitary Scaling.

The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dekh bhai, Mangoes aur Apples dono ke events bilkul independent hain. Exam me variable `X` dekh kar ghabrana nahi hai. Sabse best hack hai ki pehle individual fruits ki total sankhya percentage ya ratio se nikal lo, aur last me unko add karke `X+50` se equate kar do. Tune jo 3 methods diye hain, aao sabka post-mortem karte hain.

Method 1 (Percentage Base Shift - Ninja Technique):
Mangoes: Let total = 100\%.
Remaining after 20\% sold = 80\%.
Remaining after 40\% of 80\% sold = 80\% \times 60\% = 48\%.
ATQ, 48\% \equiv 48 \Rightarrow 100\% \equiv 100 mangoes.

Apples: Let total = 100\%.
Sold to A = 40\%. Bacha hua 60\%.
Ab isme se 100 apples B ko diye, toh 10\% bache.
Iska sidha observation hai: 60\% - 10\% = 50\%. Ye 50\% hi 100 apples ke barabar hain!
50\% \equiv 100 \Rightarrow 100\% \equiv 200 apples.

Total fruits = 100 + 200 = 300.
So, X + 50 = 300 \Rightarrow X = 250.
Find: X + 500 = 250 + 500 = 750.

Method 2 (Fractional Successive Ratio - Exam Approach):
Mangoes (Successive Change):
20\% = \frac{1}{5} (Base shift: 5 se 4), 40\% = \frac{2}{5} (Base shift: 5 se 3).
InitialFinal
54
53
2512
12 units \equiv 48 \Rightarrow 1 unit = 4.
Total Mangoes = 25 \times 4 = 100.

Apples (Direct Observation):
Total = 100\%. Sold to A = 40\%, Remaining = 10\%.
Consumed percentage without absolute value = 40\% + 10\% = 50\%.
Rest 50\% is exactly the 100 apples given to B.
50\% \equiv 100 \Rightarrow 100\% = 200.
Total = 300, X = 250, Ans = 750.

Method 3 (Basic Variable Equation - The Trap):
Ye teri 3rd image wala approach hai, jo ekdum basic hai. Exam me ye nahi lagana hai!
Mangoes = 100 (derived). Total fruits = X + 50.
So, Total Apples = (X + 50) - 100 = (X - 50).
ATQ for apples:
Sold 40\% (i.e. \frac{2}{5}), remaining = \frac{3}{5}.
(X - 50) \times \frac{3}{5} - 100 = (X - 50) \times \frac{1}{10}
(X - 50) \times \frac{3}{5} - (X - 50) \times \frac{1}{10} = 100
(X - 50) \times \frac{1}{2} = 100
(X - 50) = 200 \Rightarrow X = 250.
Bhai, isme expression balance karne me time jayega. It's a pure waste of 30-40 seconds.


Future Exam Takeaway (Hack Observation):
Exam me hamesha Method 1 ya 2 lagana hai. Jab question me do alag-alag items (Mangoes aur Apples) ho, toh starting ke combined variable (X+50) ko temporarily bhool jao. Individual parts ko 100\% base ya ratio base par solve karo, unki real values nikal kar last me combine karo. Variables ke jaal me tab tak nahi fasna jab tak strictly necessary na ho!

questions_hin.q_hi: Khushi scores $33.33\%$ in an examination and after review, even though her score is increased by $40\%$, she fails by 10 marks. If her post - review score is increased by $14.28\%$, she will have 10 marks more than the passing score. Find the percentage score needed for passing the examination.
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, fraction ka khel hai. $33.33\%$ matlab $\frac{1}{3}$, $40\%$ matlab $\frac{2}{5}$ aur $14.28\%$ matlab $\frac{1}{7}$. Base aisi value maan jo in sabse kat jaye, jaise $300$! Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total marks $300$ maan le. Khushi ka score aaya $100$ unit. Usme $40\%$ badhaya toh ban gaya $140$ unit. Ye passing marks se $10$ kam hai. Passing = $140u + 10$. Phir is $140u$ ko $14.28\%$ (yani $\frac{1}{7}$) badhaya, toh $140 + 20 = 160$ unit hua. Ye passing se $10$ jyada hai. Passing = $160u - 10$. Equate karega toh $140u + 10 = 160u - 10 \implies 20u = 20 \implies u = 1$. Total marks $300$ hue. Passing marks $140 + 10 = 150$ hue. Ye $300$ ka exactly $50\%$ hai. Bawal trick hai ye! Method 2 (Concept Builder): Variables me khelna hai toh Total = $x$. Initial score = $\frac{x}{3}$. After first review = $\frac{x}{3} \times \frac{140}{100} = \frac{14x}{30}$. Fails by 10, toh Passing = $\frac{14x}{30} + 10$. Second review me score = $\frac{14x}{30} \times \frac{8}{7} = \frac{16x}{30}$. Passes by 10, toh Passing = $\frac{16x}{30} - 10$. Dono equations barabar kar de. Vahi $x = 300$ aayega. Mazdoori lambi hai, tu Ninja technique hi lagana exam me. Exam Takeaway: Jab multiple fractions dikhein, toh total hamesha unke denominators ka LCM maana kar!
StageScore (Units)
1. Initial ($33.33\%$)100u
2. Review 1 ($+40\%$)140u (Fail by 10)
3. Review 2 ($+14.28\%$)160u (Pass by 10)

questions_hin.q_hi: If the price of rice is raised by $28\%$, then by how much percent must a person reduce his consumption of rice so that his overall expenditure remains the same?
questions_hin.s_hi:
The "Pen-Free" Observation First:

Dekh bhai, sidha CPR (Constant Product Ratio) laga. Jab fraction $+\frac{x}{y}$ se badhti hai aur product same rakhna ho, toh factor $-\frac{x}{x+y}$ se girana padta hai.

Method 1 (CPR Ninja Technique):

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Price } \uparrow = +28\% = +\frac{28}{100} = +\frac{7}{25} \\ \text{Consumption } \downarrow = -\frac{7}{25+7} = -\frac{7}{32} \\ \% \text{ Change} = \frac{7}{32} \times 100 = \frac{175}{8} = 21.875\% $$

Exam Takeaway: General method lagaoge toh 1 minute waste hoga, CPR lagaya toh 10 second me answer. Flexi-Frac approach is deadly!

questions_hin.q_hi: For a number, greater than one, the difference between itself and its reciprocal is 20% of the sum of itself and its reciprocal. By how much percentage (nearest to an integer) is the square of the number less than its cube?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: 5. Unitary Scaling

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, language thodi ghumau hai par basic algebraic equation ban rahi hai. Cross multiply karke seedha number ka square nikal lena sabse asaan hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Equation ko fraction ki tarah set kar, solve karke cube aur square ka ratio nikal de!

Mathematically :-
$$x - \frac{1}{x} = 0.2\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right) \implies \frac{x - \frac{1}{x}}{x + \frac{1}{x}} = \frac{1}{5}$$
$$5x - \frac{5}{x} = x + \frac{1}{x} \implies 4x = \frac{6}{x} \implies x^2 = 1.5$$
$$x = \sqrt{1.5} \approx 1.2247$$
$$\text{Req } \% = \frac{x^3 - x^2}{x^3} \times 100 = \left(1 - \frac{1}{x}\right) \times 100$$
$$\left(1 - \frac{1}{1.2247}\right) \times 100 \approx (1 - 0.816) \times 100 \approx 18.3\% \approx 18\%$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Absolute values pe ja kar cube nikalega aur square nikalega toh decimals me jaakar puri tarah fass jayega. Seedha ratio utha.

Mathematically :-
$$\text{Req } \% = \frac{A-B}{A} \times 100 = \left(1 - \frac{B}{A}\right) \times 100$$

Exam Takeaway: Percentage less/more pooche algebra me toh hamesha unka ratio $\frac{A}{B}$ form me convert kar lo, original absolute values ki tension khatam ho jayegi.

List IList II
% Less of A wrt B$(1 - \frac{A}{B}) \times 100$

questions_hin.q_hi: In a school ratio of number of boys and girls is 16:9. 68.75% of boys and 44.44% of girls went for picnic. Find the percentage of total students who did not go to picnic?
questions_hin.s_hi:
**Core Conceptual Tool:** 5. Unitary Scaling

**Pen-Free Observation:** Dekh bhai, dangerous percentages ko dekhte hi unka fraction yaad aana chahiye! 68.75\% aur 44.44\% dekh kar darna nahi hai, base 16 aur 9 already hint de rahe hain ki fractions aaram se katenge.

**Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):** 68.75\% = $50\% + 18.75\% = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{3}{16} = \frac{11}{16}$. 44.44\% standard $\frac{4}{9}$ hota hai. Boys jo nahi gaye = $1 - \frac{11}{16} = \frac{5}{16}$. 16 ka $\frac{5}{16}$ = 5. Girls jo nahi gayi = $1 - \frac{4}{9} = \frac{5}{9}$. 9 ka $\frac{5}{9}$ = 5. Total nahi gaye = 10. Total strength = 25. Percentage = $\frac{10}{25} \times 100 = 40\%$.

**Method 2 (Concept Builder):** Fractions convert karke sidha remainder nikal. Agar $\frac{11}{16}$ chale gaye toh $\frac{5}{16}$ bach gaye. Arithmetic game sirf fractions ke base denominator ko target karne ka hota hai.

**Exam Takeaway:** CGL hamesha values ratio aur percentages aisi deta hai jo ek dusre ko cancel karein. Weird percentages me numerator se zyada denominator ko pakdo.

B. Girls (9)2. $9 \times \frac{5}{9} = 5$

questions_hin.q_hi: The salaries of Prashant and Sujal together amount to 24000. Prashant spends (x - 5)% of his salary and Sujal, (x + 5)% of his. If ratio of their income is 3 : 5 and their savings are same, then what is difference between their expenditure?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Tool Triggered: 5. Unitary Scaling

The "Pen-Free" Observation First:
Dekh bhai, Income ratio 3:5 hai, total 8 unit = 24000. Toh Prashant = 9000, Sujal = 15000. Dono ki saving barabar hai. Agar Income ka gap 6000 hai aur savings same hain, toh Expenditure ka gap directly Income ke gap ke barabar hoga! Calculation ki zarurat hi nahi thi!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Logic aur Common Sense.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Income (P)} = \frac{3}{8} \times 24000 = 9000 \\ \text{Income (S)} = \frac{5}{8} \times 24000 = 15000 \\ \text{Income} = \text{Exp} + \text{Sav} \\ \text{If } \text{Sav}_P = \text{Sav}_S, \text{ then:} \\ \text{Inc}_S - \text{Inc}_P = \text{Exp}_S - \text{Exp}_P \\ \text{Diff} = 15000 - 9000 = 6000 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Percentage equate karke x nikalna.

Mathematically :-
$$ \text{Sav}_P = 100 - (x - 5) = (105 - x)\% \\ \text{Sav}_S = 100 - (x + 5) = (95 - x)\% \\ 9000 \times (105 - x) = 15000 \times (95 - x) \\ 3(105 - x) = 5(95 - x) \implies 315 - 3x = 475 - 5x \\ 2x = 160 \implies x = 80 \\ \text{Exp}_P = 75\% \text{ of } 9000 = 6750 \\ \text{Exp}_S = 85\% \text{ of } 15000 = 12750 \\ \text{Diff} = 12750 - 6750 = 6000 $$

Exam Takeaway: Jab savings same ho toh Income ka difference seedha Expenditure ke difference ke barabar hota hai. x nikalna bewakoofi thi!

questions_hin.q_hi: Ridhi scored 65 marks in Mathematics. He scored $70\%$ marks in Hindi and $(X^3 + 20)$ marks in English. The maximum marks for each subject is 80. The overall percentage of marks obtained by Riddhi in all three subjects together is $70\%$. Find X?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, overall average $70\%$ hai toh har subject me target marks set kar, jo average se extra laya usko dusre subjects se balance kar le.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Deviation Balance. Mathematically :-
$$Avg_{target} = 80 \times 0.70 = 56$$
$$H = 56 \text{ (0 dev)}$$
$$M = 65 \text{ (+9 dev)}$$
$$E_{target} = 56 - 9 = 47$$
$$X^3 + 20 = 47 \Rightarrow X^3 = 27 \Rightarrow X = 3$$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Total Sum approach. Mathematically :-
$$Total = 80 \times 3 = 240$$
$$Obtained = 240 \times 0.70 = 168$$
$$65 + 56 + (X^3 + 20) = 168$$
$$141 + X^3 = 168 \Rightarrow X^3 = 27 \Rightarrow X=3$$

Exam Takeaway: Sabko add karke wapas minus karne se accha hai individual average deviation zero pe balance karna, isse calculation chhoti ho jati hai.

questions_hin.q_hi: If the height of a triangle is increased by $20\%$ and the base is increased by $12\%$, what is the new area if the old area was 200 cm$^2$?

questions_hin.q_hi: A is $33.33\%$ less than B and C is $20\%$ more than D. If D is $50\%$ more than A, then which of the following is true?
questions_hin.s_hi:
[Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change]

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, yahan percentages chain me hain. Denominators $3, 2, 5$ hain. Inka LCM 30 hota hai, toh B ko seedha 300 maan le taaki decimals ka panga hi na rahe.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
1. $B = 300$
2. A, B se $1/3$ kam hai $\Rightarrow A = 300 - 100 = 200$
3. D, A se $1/2$ zyada hai $\Rightarrow D = 200 + 100 = 300$
4. C, D se $1/5$ zyada hai $\Rightarrow C = 300 + 60 = 360$
Ab clear hai ki $C = 360$ aur $B = 300$. Ratio $\frac{C}{B} = 1.2$, toh $C = 1.2B$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Ratios likh aur multiply kar de: $\frac{A}{B} = \frac{2}{3}$, $\frac{D}{A} = \frac{3}{2}$, $\frac{C}{D} = \frac{6}{5}$.
$\frac{A}{B} \times \frac{D}{A} \times \frac{C}{D} = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{3}{2} \times \frac{6}{5} = \frac{6}{5} = 1.2$. CGL me direct ratio multiply karke time bacha!

questions_hin.q_hi: Out of total income a person's expenditure on food, cloth and other items are in the ratio of 3: 4: 3 respectively. If his expenditure is increased by 12% on food and 15% on cloth and decreased by 8% on other items. What percent should his income be increased so that no effect is recorded on the consumption of food, cloth and other items ?
questions_hin.s_hi:
Core Conceptual Tool: JSM/Deviation.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, ratios di hain 3:4:3. Inko sidha 300, 400 aur 300 maan le. Income base 1000 banega. Bas change nikal aur 1000 pe percentage fenk.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Zeroes assum kar aur base 1000 pe deviation nikal. Mathematically :-

$+ (300 \times 12\%) = +36$

$+ (400 \times 15\%) = +60$

$- (300 \times 8\%) = -24$

$\text{Net} = 36 + 60 - 24 = +72$

$\text{Inc } \% = \frac{72}{1000} \times 100 = 7.2\%$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Weighted average approach laga fraction me. Mathematically :-

$\text{Total parts} = 3+4+3 = 10$

$\text{Change} = \frac{(3 \times 12) + (4 \times 15) + (3 \times -8)}{10}$

$\text{Change} = \frac{36 + 60 - 24}{10} = \frac{72}{10} = 7.2\%$

Exam Takeaway: Jaha split ratio di ho waha zeros chipka ke life aasan kiya kar ya direct weighted average laga, fraction apne aap set hoga.
